card.title: Inverse functions and trig equations — principal vs general

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Inverse circular functions undo sin/cos/tan but must choose ONE value — the principal value in restricted ranges (sin⁻¹: [−π/2, π/2], cos⁻¹: [0, π], tan⁻¹: (−π/2, π/2)). Trigonometric equations go the other way: infinitely many solutions captured by general-value formulas with integer n. Sum/difference identities (tan(α±β)) power both.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: sin⁻¹(−½) = −π/6 (4th quadrant, in range)  ·  cos⁻¹(√3/2)+sin⁻¹(½) = π/6+π/6 = π/3  ·  tan(α±β) = (tanα±tanβ)/(1∓tanαtanβ): tanα=2,tanβ=3 → tan(α+β) = 5/(−5) = −1  ·  sinθ = 0 → θ = nπ · cosθ = 0 → θ = (2n+1)π/2

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Principal values obey their ranges strictly — sin⁻¹(−½) is −π/6, never 7π/6. General solutions need the interval stated ([0, 2π] vs all reals). tan formulas need defined denominators (α±β ≠ π/2 + kπ). Factor trig equations before splitting (2sin²θ − sinθ − 1 = (2sinθ+1)(sinθ−1)).

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: 2sin²θ − sinθ − 1 = 0 → sinθ = 1 or −½ → θ = π/2, 7π/6, 11π/6 in [0, 2π] (NEB 2023, 4 marks). tanα = 2, tanβ = 3: tan(α+β) = −1, verified via sin/cos expansion (NEB 2024, 3 marks). sin⁻¹x + cos⁻¹x = π/2 collapses pairs instantly.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Solve 2sin²θ − sinθ − 1 = 0, θ ∈ [0, 2π]: factor → (2sinθ + 1)(sinθ − 1) = 0 → sinθ = −½ (θ = 7π/6, 11π/6) or sinθ = 1 (θ = π/2). Three solutions, each checked against the interval (NEB 2023, 4 marks). Principal-value warm-ups: sin⁻¹(−½) = −π/6 (NEB 2024).

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Inverse notation sin⁻¹x is NOT 1/sin x — the −1 means inverse function, and it traps every cohort. Principal values discard infinitely many valid angles; general formulas recover them only with correct n-parametrisation. Identities assume defined expressions (no division by cos = 0).

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: General values from the unit circle: sinθ = k fixes two symmetric points per revolution → θ = nπ + (−1)ⁿα; cosθ = k gives θ = 2nπ ± α by even symmetry; tanθ = k gives θ = nπ + α by π-periodicity. tan(α+β) falls out of sin/cos addition divided through by cosαcosβ.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Equations: factor first (quadratic in sin/cos/tan), solve each factor, filter by interval. Principal values: locate the quadrant, land in range. Pair sin⁻¹+cos⁻¹ of complementary values → π/2. Draw the CAST circle before writing any angle.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: NEB 2024 (2): principal value sin⁻¹(−1/2). NEB 2024 (3): tanα = 2, tanβ = 3 — tan(α±β) + verify. NEB 2023 (2): cos⁻¹(√3/2) + sin⁻¹(1/2). NEB 2023 (4): 2sin²θ − sinθ − 1 = 0 on [0, 2π].
